I am sorry that you are unhappy with the service we gave you when you called on Friday. 

Our reception team work under strict guidelines set by the GP Partners that determine the urgency of the appointment needed. I have reviewed the reason for your appointment and I can confirm that the receptionist did follow these instructions. Urgent appointments are for medically urgent problems which must be dealt with that day and if a matter is not medically urgent, a routine appointment is offered. This protects the urgent appointments for those who do need them. We too are unhappy with the wait for routine appointments. General Practice funding does now allow for us to employ more GPs to reduce the waiting times but we continue to campaign for this alongside the British Medical Association. 

I do not agree that our receptionists are unprofessional, nor that they are disrespectful to those whose first languages is not English. Our team work hard to ensure they help all patients as much as possible and I receive many compliments every day about the service they provide. So I am very sorry that this was not your experience too. 

Kind regards

Rachel Stark

I am sorry you are unhappy with us. I will take your points in order and hope I can address many of these.

The Car Park. We agree that the parking is limited. The NHS only funds a certain amount of spaces, and of course we are limited by the footprint too. We do all we can to maximise the spaces - lots of the staff don't drive to work, we have an offsite staff car park, and Wickes have given permission to use their car park (up to the allowed limit). We do raise it at every NHS review and will continue to do so.

Our wait for routine appointments is 4-8 weeks at the moment. Longer waiting times are long across the vast majority of the NHS at the moment due to demand and need exceeding supply due to underfunding and a depleting workforce. We work hard to provide safe, quality and continuity of care to do the best we can within the resources available. We too want shorter waiting times and campaign for this with the BMA Collective Actions and publicity.

I can confirm we have had EMIS since 1989 and were one of the first practices nationally to embrace paperless working shortly after. We recently had to change to EMIS for appointments when the other provider Informatica withdrew from the market.
In Somerset Musgrove use TQuest, the path IT system, but it too is withdrawing from the market and hence all of Somerset services - GPs, Hospital etc - are moving to the other pathology IT system - ICE - in November. The functionality is very similar across both systems.

I think your remaining concerns relate to your experience of the Doctors. If you would like to contact me directly about this, I am happy to discuss this. Obviously your medical history is not something I want to discuss on here but I do want to help you.
